subject: botany
question_text: What is meant by monosporic development of the female gametophyte?

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack botany section (book p.17, VSAQ 2). Botany holds only ONE source book — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no botany board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. The book's answer line is garbled ('Development of embryosac from single functional megaspore in monosporic typic'); this card writes the standard sentence.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question
Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants · 2 marks

steps.label: Four megaspores, one functional
lines: The megaspore mother cell divides by meiosis
Three of them degenerate; only one remains
steps.why: Monosporic means 'from one spore'. To say that clearly, first show that meiosis made four megaspores and only one survives — the definition then follows by itself.
common_mistakes: Writing mitosis for the megaspore mother cell division — it is meiosis.
Saying all four megaspores form embryo sacs — three degenerate.
steps.memory_tip: Mono = one. Four are made, three die, ONE builds the embryo sac.
steps.margin_note: Two short sentences: meiosis gives four, one stays functional.

steps.label: Definition

lines.text: Embryo sac from ONE functional megaspore

lines: Development of the embryo sac from a single
steps.why: The boxed line is the definition the examiner scans for; the Polygonum type is the standard monosporic embryo sac, so the example anchors the term.
common_mistakes: Defining it as development from one 'microspore' — that is the male side; here it is the megaspore.
Leaving out 'functional' — the one that survives is the functional megaspore.
steps.memory_tip: MEGAspore → female gametophyte; MICROspore → male. Monosporic = the female sac from one megaspore.
steps.margin_note: The boxed definition plus the Polygonum example is the complete 2-mark answer.

insider_note: Write 'megaspore', not 'microspore' — one letter swap here is the difference between the female and the male gametophyte, and examiners do not give the mark for the wrong one.
